note: Events that belong to contracts (S3.4, D-115): the basic inspection at a checkpoint, which comes before any other checkpoint event while contraband is aboard (`priority`), and the salvage claims (one for each salvage contract), each of which opens whenever we stand at the claim point with the claim unworked. The format is described at the top of src/narrative/events.js.

items.title: Inspection at {place}
items.text: A Receivers cutter holds the lane with its lights on. The officer on the channel wants a scanner team aboard and the hold opened, and is polite about it in the way of someone who does not have to be.

choices.label: Open the hold and let them look

outcomes.text: They go straight to the crates you least wanted them to open, as if someone told them where to look. The crates leave on their cutter, and a fine is written up on the spot.
The scanner team is two boys and a handheld with a cracked screen. They read the stencils on the crates aloud, tick a box, and leave.

choices.label: Make the scanner team's afternoon easier

outcomes.text: The officer counts it twice, logs the ship as inspected, and wishes you a safe crossing in a voice that means it for exactly as long as the transfer takes.
The officer takes the money, thanks you for it, and sends the scanner team anyway.

choices.label: Put someone on the channel who can talk

outcomes.text: {voice} reads the officer a clause from the company's own transit charter, slowly. Nobody on that cutter wants to be the one who looks it up. The lane clears.
{voice} talks well, and the officer listens, and sends the scanner team anyway.

choices.label: Burn through the line before they board

outcomes.text: The cutter is slow to turn. By the time it has, you are a heat trace and a name on a list.
The cutter was waiting for exactly that.

items.title: The claim at {place}
items.text: The Aphelion turns slowly where the claim token says she will be, an ore tender with her lights out and her airlock cut open. The cut marks are still bright. Somebody has been here, and not long ago.

outcomes.text: It takes the whole watch. The crew come back black to the elbows with four crates of salvage and nothing worse than a cut hand.
You are three crates in when a ship comes round her hull with its guns out, and a voice on the channel says the claim is theirs.
{cutter} opens the sealed bay in twenty minutes with a cutting rig and a lot of language. Everything worth taking is in there, packed and tagged by whoever ran out of time before you.

choices.label: Take what is near the lock and go

outcomes.text: Two crates from the lock bay, and you are gone before anyone else arrives. The rest of her stays where she is.
You log her position again. The claim will keep. Whoever cut that airlock may not wait as long.

items.title: The Hollow Psalm at {place}
items.text: The Order's chapel ship hangs nose-down in the lane with her lamps still burning on a battery that should have died years ago. The claim token opens her outer door without argument. Inside, the bells are wrapped in quilting and strapped to the deck, as if someone meant to come back for them.

choices.label: Carry the bells out one at a time

outcomes.text: It is slow, heavy work in a cold that gets into the joints. Three crates, three bells, and nobody drops one.
The second bell rings once against a bulkhead on the way out. Every lamp on the chapel ship goes off at the same moment. You take the third crate anyway, and nobody talks on the way back.

choices.label: Rig a sling and float them across

outcomes.text: {rigger} strings a line between the two locks and runs the crates across it like washing. The whole thing takes an hour and the bells never touch metal.

choices.label: Take the nearest bell and go

outcomes.text: One crate, from just inside the door. The other two stay where the Order left them, under their quilts.
You close her door behind you. The lamps are still burning when the range opens.

items.title: The relay buoy at {place}
items.text: The buoy is where the Receivers said it would be, which is to say in the worst of {hazard}. Its recorder housing is three sealed drums bolted to a frame that has been taking hits for a long time.

choices.label: Suit up and unbolt the drums

outcomes.text: Forty minutes outside with a wrench and a tether. All three drums come aboard, and so does a good deal of the hazard, on the suits.
The drums come free easily. The frame comes free too, and swings into the hull on the way past.

choices.label: Hold the ship steady in the lee of the buoy

outcomes.text: {pilot} parks the ship so close to the buoy that the crew can reach the drums from the lock. Nobody goes outside.

choices.label: Cut the nearest drum loose and go

outcomes.text: One drum, cut free at the bracket. The other two will have to wait for another ship or another day.
You back out of the hazard with the buoy still blinking behind you.
